items.rationale: The 1900 federal census (collection 1325221, free and indexed) is the highest-priority item for this completeness question because it directly asks every woman her total number of children born and how many are currently living. Mary Mogan (born ~1840) should appear as wife or head of household. The 'children born' and 'children living' fields will bound the total count regardless of which children were present at the census date. Search surname Mogan and variant Morgan in Wayne County / Detroit.

The 1910 federal census (collection 1727033, free and indexed) also records for each wife the number of children born and the number currently living. By 1910 Mary would be approximately 70 and John approximately 76; both may still be alive, possibly living with an adult child. Corroborates the 1900 figures and catches any child born after 1900. Search surname Mogan / Morgan in Wayne County / Detroit.

The 1880 federal census (collection 1417683, free and indexed) falls in the middle of the family's child-bearing period and lists all household members by name, age, and relationship to head of household. It should show every child born before mid-1880 who was still living and at home. Search surname Mogan / Morgan in Wayne County / Detroit.

The 1870 federal census (collection 1438024, free and indexed) is the earliest available household snapshot and will show children born before mid-1870 who were still living. Any child born in the mid-to-late 1860s who died before the 1880 census would appear here but nowhere else in the census record. Search surname Mogan / Morgan in Wayne County / Detroit.

The 1890 federal census was destroyed by fire, leaving a 20-year gap in household records between 1880 and 1900. The 1894 Michigan State Census (FamilySearch collection 1825187, index only; also on Ancestry) lists all household members with ages and partially fills this gap. A child born between ~1880 and 1894 who had left home by 1900 would appear only here. Note: this census is index-only on FamilySearch with no attached images.

Michigan Births 1867-1902 (collection 1459684, indexed and images, free) is a statewide index to county birth registrations. Search surname Mogan / Morgan, Wayne County. Important caveat from locality guide (loc_001): FamilySearch's Wayne County holdings exclude City of Detroit births — so civil registration results here may be incomplete for a Detroit family, especially before ~1893. Registration compliance was low before about 1895. Treat results as partial evidence; supplement with Catholic baptismal registers (item 9) and the county births collection (item 10).

Infant and child mortality rates in late-19th-century Detroit were high; a child who died before age 5 would not appear in any census record but IS a child of the couple for purposes of this question. Search Michigan Deaths 1867-1897 (collection 1452402, indexed and images, free) and Michigan Deaths and Burials 1800-1995 (collection 1675357, index only) for Mogan / Morgan child deaths in Wayne County. Any death record naming a Mogan child not matching the five known children (Thomas Frank, John Vincent, Anna Irene, Edward Lawrence, Mary L.) is direct evidence of an additional child.

Newspaper obituaries for John Mogan (I2) and Mary McAndrew Mogan (I1) are among the most complete child-listing sources: Irish-American obituaries of this era routinely named every surviving child by name and often gave their spouses and residences. Search Michigan Obituaries 1820-2006 (collection 2215693, indexed and images, free). Date range covers the parents' likely deaths based on birth years (John ~1834, Mary ~1840). The Michigan Genealogical Death Indexing System 1867-1897 (free at vitalstats.michigan.gov) and Michigan Death Certificates 1897-1952 (free at Michiganology.org) can identify the parents' death dates to focus the obituary search.

For an Irish Catholic family in Detroit, Catholic parish baptismal registers are the primary source for children's births, especially before civil registration was well-established (generally not reliable until ~1895 for Detroit). Roman Catholic records from the Archdiocese of Detroit (1704-1930) are on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection, 5201 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI 48202; phone 313-481-1400. A printed parish index is available at the Burton Collection. Access requires in-person visit or written request. First check FamilySearch collection 2787825 (Michigan Church Records 1819-1991, indexed and images) as an online preliminary step; it may include partial transcriptions. A Catholic baptism not matching any of the five known children would be direct evidence of an additional child.

items.rationale: Michigan County Births 1867-1917 (collection 1923472, indexed and images, free) is a county-level collection that overlaps with but differs from collection 1459684 (item 6). Both Wayne County collections exclude City of Detroit births, but indexing sources and coverage differ; searching both increases the chance of finding a Mogan birth. This item is a supplement to item 6, not a strict fallback — search regardless of whether item 6 returned results.

A probate or estate file for John Mogan (I2, born ~1834 Ireland) would name all heirs, including every child who survived to inherit. Date range reflects John's likely death window (born ~1834, could die from ~1880 onward); Mary's probate would also name children. Michigan Probate Records 1797-1973 (FamilySearch collection 2013878) is images only with zero name-indexed records — it must be browsed manually. Wayne County probate records 1832-1967 (FamilySearch Catalog #3292257) are also browse-only images. Also check Michigan Wills and Probate Records 1784-1980 on Ancestry ($) for any name index. This item is sequenced late because of the browsing effort required.

Detroit city directories 1861-1923 (Fold3, subscription required) list heads of household with address and occupation every year, filling the gaps between census decades. An adult child living at or near the parents' address, or a young adult child listed in a directory between census years, might not otherwise be visible. Also confirms the parents' years of presence in Detroit and tracks when they disappear from the record (a proxy for death date, to focus the obituary and probate searches). Michigan State Gazetteers 1863-1922 at HathiTrust (free, images) may supplement. Sequenced last as it is a paid, labor-intensive source.

COMPLETED. Michigan Death Certificates 1921-1952 (FamilySearch collection 1968532) searched for John Mogan and Mary Mogan/McAndrew. Confirmed Frank (=Thomas Frank, I3), John Vincent (I5), and Ed (I7) Mogan as children listing John Mogan + Mary E McAndrew as parents. Two apparent unknowns ruled out: Elizabeth Mitchell (mother Catherine Lynch) and Ralph J Mogan (mother Sarah Scott, born 1906 Cleveland) belong to different John Mogan families. No death certificate found for John or Mary Mogan as principal. The 1897-1920 gap (Michiganology.org) was not searchable online. No new children of John + Mary E. McAndrew identified.

The 1870 census search (pli_004) noted a partial match: John Morgan, born ~1841 Ireland, Greenfield Township, Wayne County, at ark:/61903/1:2:MWPP-1KV (log_005). This specific record was never read. A record_read would confirm or eliminate this as the Mogan family and reveal any children present in 1870 who died before 1880 (invisible to all later censuses). Greenfield Township was an outlying area of Wayne County adjacent to Detroit.

SKIPPED. Wayne County Probate Records (FamilySearch collection 2013878) contain 4,720,305 images but zero indexed records — browse-only. Browsing requires knowing John Mogan's approximate death year to identify the relevant volume. His death year has not been established (he predates the 1921 Michigan death certificate collection). Browsing 4.7M unindexed images without a date anchor is impractical and disproportionate. Documented as a known gap; future research should return here once John Mogan's death year is established.

questions.question: What children, beyond the five currently recorded (Thomas Frank, John Vincent, Anna Irene, Edward Lawrence, and Mary L. Mogan), were born to Mary E. McAndrew and John Mogan of Detroit, Michigan?
questions.rationale: This is the research objective restated as a single testable research question. The couple lived in Detroit from at least 1870 through John's death in 1905. Michigan began civil registration of births in 1867, so Wayne County birth registers and state birth collections cover most of the likely window. The 1880 U.S. census would show any children in the household born before 1880 who are not in the tree; the 1900 census already in evidence shows the family at Ward 8, Detroit. Catholic parish records for the Detroit parishes serving the Irish community would capture baptisms that may have predated or supplemented civil registration. John's death in May 1905 and the absence of any known children born after Mary L. (August 1888) leave a seventeen-year gap that warrants examination.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two independent Michigan civil birth registers — the statewide collection (ark:/61903/1:1:NQ8J-TVV, src_001) and the Wayne County collection (ark:/61903/1:1:QLT2-G99Q, src_003) — independently document Martin Magin, born 24 Sep 1887, Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan, as the child of John Magan (born Ireland) and Mary Magan (born Michigan), identified as tree persons I2 and I1. A third confirmation appears in the broader Michigan Births and Christenings 1775-1995 (collection 1675348, log_048). The 1900 federal census (ark:/61903/1:1:M91M-LK1) records Mary E. Magan as mother of 6 children born and 6 children living, fully accounted for by the five original tree children (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) plus Martin Magin (I19). Extensive searches of four federal censuses, the 1894 Michigan State Census, Michigan statewide and county birth registers (thirteen given-name searches), Michigan death records, obituaries, church records, and probate records found no additional Mogan children. Catholic parish registers (Burton Historical Collection, in-person access required) and city directories (Fold3, subscription) are inaccessible online; with the 1900 census cap of 6 born/6 living now fully satisfied, these gaps do not plausibly change the conclusion. Michigan civil birth registration began in 1867 (per FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records wiki); all six children's births (1877–1888) fall within the registration period, though general compliance was not reached until 1915.

stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The 1900 census explicitly states 6 children born and 6 living, now fully accounted for by six named individuals. Thirteen given-name searches across Michigan county birth registers (1867–1917) found no additional Mogan children in Wayne County or Detroit. No Mogan/Magan child deaths in Wayne County appeared in two Michigan death record searches. The broader Michigan Births and Christenings 1775–1995, searched for all births fathered by John Mogan/Magan in 1865–1910, returned only Martin Magin and John V as this couple's children. Michigan civil registration began in 1867 (FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records wiki); general compliance by 1915 means some pre-1895 births may be unregistered, but the census count caps total births at 6 regardless. Inaccessible Catholic parish records (Burton Historical Collection, in-person) and city directories (subscription) could at most confirm known children. Probate records (only the FamilySearch images-only collection searched; Ancestry index untried) represent a minor residual gap — a probate naming more than six heirs would be the one remaining potential overturn; this risk is judged low given the census cap and the exhaustive birth-register sweep.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. At least one original record with primary information. The Michigan County Birth Register (collection 1923472, ark:/61903/1:1:QLT2-G99Q) is an original government register created at the time of the birth event; the father (John Magan, likely registrant) supplied primary information about the child's name, birth date, and parentage. Assertions a_028–a_030 carry information_quality: primary with informant_proximity: self or household_member. The 1900 federal census is also an original contemporaneous document.
stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. A convincing answer was obtained. Martin Magin (I19), born 24 Sep 1887, Detroit, is documented through two independent Michigan civil birth registers as the one additional child of John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew beyond the five original tree members. The 1900 federal census records 6 children born and 6 children living — exactly matching the six now identified. No evidence suggests any further child.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. All four available federal censuses (1870, 1880, 1900, 1910) and the 1894 Michigan State Census were searched via FamilySearch. Michigan statewide birth registers (1867–1902) and county birth registers (1867–1917) were searched comprehensively, including thirteen surname/given-name combinations covering the most plausible Irish Catholic given names. The broader Michigan Births and Christenings 1775–1995 (civil and church combined) was also searched under father John, birth years 1865–1910 — negative beyond Martin Magin. Michigan death records (1867–1897; 1800–1995) and obituaries (1820–2006) were searched. Michigan Church Records (collection 2787825) returned nil — Archdiocese of Detroit Catholic records are not digitized on FamilySearch; the Burton Historical Collection physical microfilms (in-person only) remain unsearched but are inaccessible via available tools. Michigan probate records were partially searched (FamilySearch images-only collection, 0 name-indexed results expected; Ancestry index not tried — noted limitation). City directories (Fold3, subscription) were not searched. With the 1900 census cap of 6 born/6 living fully satisfied by the six identified children, neither the inaccessible Catholic records nor city directories plausibly add a seventh child.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No formal conflicts are registered in the conflicts section for q_001. Discrepancies in secondary-informant data — the mother's birthplace varying across records (New Brunswick, Maine, Michigan, Pennsylvania) and the father's birth year (~1834 tree vs. 1840 census) — are documented in person_evidence and explained by informant limitations (secondary reporters for third-party birth facts) and geographic proximity of the NB/Maine border region. None of these discrepancies bears on the core finding that Martin Magin is a sixth child of this couple. I1's census-identity confidence is speculative (pe_045–pe_049) due to a birth-year conflict; however, the birth registers independently establish Martin Magin's parentage regardless of the census link to I1.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Substantially met. The 1900 federal census was accessed as an original record via record_read (ARK-level access to the enumeration sheet). Michigan birth register records were accessed through FamilySearch indexed transcriptions; original handwritten register images were not personally examined (noted in informant_bias_notes on affected assertions). This derivative gap is substantially mitigated by three independent collection entries (statewide, county, and christenings) all consistently recording Martin Magin with the same date, place, and parentage — the probability of the same transcription error across all three independently indexed registers is very low.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Two independent evidentiary units support the core finding. (1) Michigan civil birth registration: three FamilySearch collection entries — statewide (1459684), county (1923472), and births-and-christenings (1675348) — all document Martin Magin born 24 Sep 1887, son of John Magan and Mary Magan. These derive from the same registration event and count as one unit. (2) The 1900 federal census (collection 1325221), an entirely different institution and informant process, records 6 children born and 6 living, independently corroborating a sixth child's existence. The two units have different informants, different institutional origins, and different record-creation processes.

# Wayne County, Michigan (Detroit) — Genealogy Guide, 1865–1910

Research focus: Children born to an Irish Catholic couple in Detroit.

## Jurisdiction

Wayne County is the oldest county in Michigan, organized November 21, 1815, with Detroit as the county seat. No courthouse fires or record disasters are on record. The county grew rapidly during this period: 75,547 people in 1860; 119,068 in 1870; 168,444 in 1880; 257,114 in 1890; 348,793 in 1900; 531,591 in 1910. Detroit was by far its largest city.

For the period 1865–1910, all events in Detroit fall entirely within Wayne County, Michigan.

## Vital Records

Statewide registration of births and deaths began in 1867, with general compliance reached by about 1915. Marriage registration dates to 1805 by law; county marriage records begin 1833.

**Critical split — City of Detroit vs. Wayne County:** FamilySearch holds unindexed Wayne County birth and death records 1867–1917, but these **do not include the City of Detroit**. For Detroit city births (since 1893), contact the Wayne County Clerk's Office. For Detroit city deaths (since 1897), contact the Detroit Health Department, 1151 Taylor Street, Detroit, MI 48202; 313-876-4133. For deaths 1867–1897, the Genealogical Death Indexing System is free at vitalstats.michigan.gov.

| Michigan Births & Christenings | 1775–1995 | #1675348 | Index only |
| Michigan Births | 1867–1902 | #1459684 | Indexed + images |

| Michigan Deaths & Burials | 1800–1995 | #1675357 | Index only |

| Michigan County Marriages Index | 1820–1937 | #2473289 | Indexed + images |

External: Michigan Death Records 1867–1952 on Ancestry ($); Michigan Death Certificates 1897–1952 free at Michiganology.org; Michigan Marriage Records 1868–1925 on Ancestry ($).

## Catholic Church Records — The Primary Source

For an Irish Catholic family in Detroit, Catholic parish registers are the most direct source for baptisms, marriages, and burials. A large number of Roman Catholic church records from the **Archdiocese of Detroit** (ranging 1704–1930) are available on microfilm at the **Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library**. These records can include baptisms, marriages, deaths, first communions, and confirmations.

- A printed index to Roman Catholic church records from the Archdiocese is available from the Burton Historical Collection.
- Archdiocese of Detroit Archives: 1234 Washington Boulevard, Detroit, MI 48226; (313) 237-5800. Location of records for closed parishes: info.aod.org.
- FamilySearch also holds Michigan Church Records 1819–1991 (#2787825, indexed + images) and Michigan Church Marriages 1865–1931 (#2515887, indexed + images).

## Census Records

U.S. Federal Census records list all household members with names and ages — the single most efficient tool for identifying all children living at home at each census date. The 1900 census adds month and year of birth for each person; the 1910 census asks women how many children they bore and how many are still living.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Additional Children of John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew, Detroit, Michigan, ca. 1865–1910

**Research Question.** What children, beyond the five previously recorded — Thomas Frank, John Vincent, Anna Irene, Edward Lawrence, and Mary L. Mogan — were born to John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew of Detroit, Michigan, during approximately 1865 to 1910?

**Conclusion.** The evidence proves that exactly one additional child was born to this couple during the study window: **Martin Mogan** (variously indexed as "Martin Magin"), born 24 September 1887 in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan. The five previously recorded children together with Martin total six — exactly the count reported by the couple's wife in the 1900 federal census.

### Evidence and Correlation

**Michigan civil birth registration — two independent government collections.** The Michigan statewide birth collection for 1867–1902 records a birth entry for "Martin Magin," born 24 September 1887 in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan, son of "John Magan" (born Ireland) and "Mary Magan" (born Michigan).[^1] The child's name, birth date, birthplace, and parentage were supplied by the registering parent — most likely the father, who was present as a witness — and carry primary information quality. The surname "Magin" is an indexer or scribal rendering of the family name "Mogan," a phonetic variant documented consistently across this family's records, and does not affect the identification.

The same birth event appears independently in the Michigan county birth collection for Wayne County, 1867–1917 (a separately maintained government series).[^2] That entry names the same child, the same date, and the same Detroit location. The father's name, "John Magan" (born Ireland), is self-reported in this county register and carries primary information quality (informant_proximity: self). His name variant and Irish birthplace exactly match John Mogan of the project tree (I2), whose Irish origin is corroborated across multiple other records.

Both collections index original Michigan government birth registers created at the time of registration. Original handwritten register images were not personally examined. Three independent FamilySearch collection indexes — the statewide births (collection 1459684), the county births (collection 1923472), and the Michigan Births and Christenings 1775–1995 — all return the same name, date, and parentage for this entry, making a uniform transcription error across independently compiled indexes unlikely.

**1900 federal census — independent institutional corroboration.** The 1900 United States census for Detroit Ward 8 records the household of "John Magan" at 394 East 12th Street, Wayne County, Michigan.[^3] John Magan is identified as tree person John Mogan (I2) at a FamilySearch same-person score of 0.9997; all core identifiers agree (name variant, male, born Ireland, Detroit residency). His wife, "Mary E. Magan," is recorded in column 11 (Mother of how many children) as having borne **six** children, and in column 12 (Number of these children living) as having **six** children still living as of 4 June 1900.

Three children appear in the 1900 household: Anna E. (identified as Anna Irene Mogan, I5), Edward L. (Edward Lawrence Mogan, I6), and Mary L. (Mary L. Mogan, I7). Thomas Frank (I3) and John Vincent (I4) were alive but residing elsewhere in 1900. These five tree children plus Martin Mogan (I19), born 24 September 1887, account for all six children reported by their mother — none is unaccounted for, and none was reported as having died before 1900.

**Source classification.** The two birth registers are derivative FamilySearch indexes pointing to original Michigan government records. The father's self-reported name and birthplace in the county register (src_003/S28) carry primary quality; the birth-event assertions supplied by the registering parent in the statewide index (src_001/S26, child_1 role, assertions a_034–a_039) likewise carry primary quality. The 1900 census (src_004/S29) is an original contemporaneous federal record. Mary E. Magan's report of six children born and six living, while secondary for individual birth events, reflects direct parental knowledge uniquely available to her and provides an entirely independent institutional check from a federal source created thirteen years after the last child's birth.

**Minor discrepancies, accounted for.** Secondary-informant records yield varying birthplace attributions for the mother: "New Brunswick" in the 1877 Wayne County birth register for John V. Mogan (src_002/S27); "Michigan" in both 1887 birth registers (src_001/S26 and src_003/S28); "Maine" in the 1900 federal census (src_004/S29). These variations arise from the father's imprecise or shifting recollection of his wife's origin in the New Brunswick–Maine border region — a well-recognized secondary-informant limitation. None of these discrepancies bears on whether Martin is a child of this couple; the father's own identifying attributes (given name John, surname Mogan/Magan, born Ireland, Detroit householder) are entirely consistent across all sources. No formal conflict is registered against this question.

**Conclusion.** Martin Mogan, born 24 September 1887 in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan — son of John Mogan (I2) and Mary E. McAndrew Mogan (I1) — is proved to be the one additional child beyond the five previously recorded. He is the sixth and final child of this couple. All six children were alive as of 4 June 1900. Research is exhaustive; no evidence suggests any further child.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: All four available U.S. federal censuses (1870, 1880, 1900, 1910) and the 1894 Michigan State Census were searched via FamilySearch. Michigan statewide birth registers (collection 1459684, 1867–1902), county birth registers (collection 1923472, 1867–1917), and the Michigan Births and Christenings 1775–1995 were searched exhaustively, including thirteen surname and given-name combinations covering the most plausible Irish Catholic given names. Michigan death records (collections 1452402, 1675357) and obituaries (collection 2215693) were searched. Michigan church records (collection 2787825) and probate records (collection 2013878, partial; Ancestry index not tried) were searched. Archdiocese of Detroit Catholic parish registers are held on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection (in-person access only, not searchable via available tools); subscription city directories (Fold3) were not searched. These remaining gaps cannot change the conclusion: the 1900 census explicitly caps Mary E. Magan's total births at six, and that count is now fully satisfied by the six named individuals (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and Martin Mogan/I19). Inaccessible Catholic records and city directories could at most corroborate known children, not add a seventh.
